compatibility: format 1.x manifests restore under this release; another major is refused before any write; the catalog copy keeps the current session catalog schema and only drops derived projection tables
drill_status: partial: the deliberately missing source object is irrecoverable; a set without it drills verified
evidence_class: mocked: a SQLite catalog file, local content addressed object folders and fixture bytes stand in for the central database, the archive bucket, the backup bucket, the hosted ledger, the swarm Redis and the brain export; a deterministic hash embedder rebuilds vectors and a fake clock measures time; no Pod, bucket or database runs

fixture_inputs.brain_backup: a brain export copied beside the ledger and coordination snapshot, each under its own key id
fixture_inputs.catalog_backup: a session catalog with two retained sessions, copied without its chunk and vector projections
fixture_inputs.immutable_objects: content addressed archive objects for every session batch and the fixture task checkpoint
fixture_inputs.missing_source_object: the second archive object of the lost session, deleted from the source store before capture

interfaces: scripts.swarm_v2.backup.capture copies the catalog without projections, the ledger, the coordination snapshot, the brain export and every archive and checkpoint object into a content addressed backup store and returns the manifest digest as the set id

scripts.swarm_v2.backup.restore refuses an unsupported format major, a grant for another corpus, an absent key id, an unaccepted component version and a folder holding other data before writing, and resumes into its own marked folder
scripts.swarm_v2.backup.rebuild rebuilds chunk and vector projections from the restored events
scripts.swarm_v2.backup.drill restores, rebuilds, answers the agreed query, recovers the designated checkpoint and reports backup_restore_verification_status
scripts.swarm_v2.backup.Registry record, drill (runs the drill itself under an attempt number), accepted, preserved, retention_allowed and status
metrics: backup_restore_verification_status per drill report, and Registry.status reports counts per status with retention_allowed

outcomes.accepted: a drill status stored by Registry.drill under a higher attempt number
outcomes.committed: the backup set manifest and its objects in the content addressed backup store
outcomes.externally_verified: none; no deployed catalog, bucket, ledger, Redis or brain was backed up or restored
outcomes.observed: case outputs in the a, b and c result files from the focused fixture run

recovery_measurement: recovery_point is the set capture time and recovery_time_seconds is measured by the drill clock; the fixture clock steps 2.5 seconds per read, so 5.0 seconds is a fixture value, not a live measurement
remaining_limitations: Encryption is the storage layer's job; the module records key ids and checks them against a keyring but encrypts nothing.
No scheduler captures sets or runs drills; a caller invokes capture and drill.
Ledger, coordination and brain components are opaque bytes from their exporters; no live exporter is wired in.
A partial set stays accepted with its irrecoverable objects listed, and retention stays stopped until a fully verified set exists.
The grant corpus gates a restore and its projects gate the query and rebuild; the grant principal is not checked against an operator role because no stored grant exists for backup sets.
The capturer chooses the historical query; query_sha256 binds the restored answer to the answer at capture, so it detects drift and loss after capture, not a wrong query chosen at capture.
No deletion path exists; a retention collector must consult Registry.retention_allowed and Registry.preserved.
Capture records the exports it is given under one capture time; taking them under one fence is the caller's job.
rollback_rehearsal: C recorded a newer set as uploaded only, so retention_allowed turned false and preserved named the drilled set; a re-drill after damaging its brain component failed, the set lost acceptance and preserved still named it
supported_versions: backup format 1.x; component versions the caller lists in Access.versions
